'''Marcus Landry''' (born November 1, 1985) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and other leagues. Landry attended [[Harold S. Vincent High School|Vincent High School]] in [[Milwaukee]], Wisconsin and played [[college basketball]] at the [[Wisconsin Badgers basketball|University of Wisconsin]] from 2005 to 2009.<ref name="Badgers">{{cite news|title=Marcus Landry bio |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/marcus_landry_857390.html |access-date=March 6, 2010 |work=UWBadgers.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029190852/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/marcus_landry_857390.html |archive-date=October 29, 2013 }}</ref>

==High school career==
Landry attended Harold S. Vincent High School where he averaged 16.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and shot 59 percent from the field as a senior, leading his team to the Division I state title game and earning him a unanimous first-team all-state selection by the Associated Press.<ref name="Badgers" />

==College career==
After graduating from high school, Landry attended the [[Wisconsin Badgers basketball|University of Wisconsin-Madison]]. He became the 33rd player in Wisconsin history to reach the 1,000-point plateau and finished his career 25th on the school's all-time scoring list with 1,114 career points and eighth in Badgers annals with 185 offensive rebounds. With 99 career blocked shots, Landry also finished fifth in Wisconsin history and was also the 18th player in the school's history with at least 1,000 points and 500 rebounds. Landry appeared in 105 straight games and started the final 75 games of his career, being part of 100 wins during his collegiate career. He had 45 career double-digit scoring games.<ref name="Badgers" /> Landry helped lead the Badgers to a [[2008 Big Ten men's basketball tournament]] championship, being named [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player]].

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Landry was signed by the [[New York Knicks]] in September 2009.

He was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] along with [[Nate Robinson]] for [[Eddie House]], [[Bill Walker (basketball)|Bill Walker]], and [[J. R. Giddens]] on February 18, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press021810-celtics-acquire-robinson.html|title=Celtics acquire Nate Robinson, Marcus Landry from Knicks |work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2010|access-date=September 22, 2013}}</ref> The Celtics assigned Landry to the [[Maine Red Claws]] on March 6, 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=Celtics' Landry assigned to NBA D-League's Red Claws|url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/03/06/celtics.landry/|access-date=March 6, 2010|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2010}}</ref>

In September 2010, he signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]], joining his brother Carl. However, he was released on October 15. He was then acquired by the Kings' [[NBA D-League]] affiliate, the [[Reno Bighorns]] for the 2010–11 season.

In July 2011, he signed a one-year deal with [[BCM Gravelines]] in [[France]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gravelines-Dunkerque signs Marcus Landry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/87466/gravelines-dunkerque-signs-marcus-landry.html|access-date=July 19, 2011|work=Sportando.com|date=July 19, 2011}}</ref> He was released soon afterwards and signed a 6-week contract with [[Bàsquet Manresa]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Assignia Manresa signs Marcus Landry with a short-term deal|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88578/assignia-manresa-signs-marcus-landry-with-a-short-term-deal.html|access-date=October 4, 2011|work=Sportando.com|date=October 4, 2011}}</ref> On December 13, 2011, he signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Phoenix Suns sign guard Ronnie Price|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8812|access-date=December 13, 2011|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 13, 2011}}</ref> but he was waived before the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]].

In July 2012, Landry signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Shanghai Sharks tab Marcus Landry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/89666/shanghai-sharks-tab-marcus-landry.html|access-date=July 1, 2012|date=July 1, 2012|work=Sportando.com}}</ref> In November 2012, he was acquired by the Reno Bighorns of the [[NBA Development League]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Full List of 2012 Returning, Affiliate and Local Tryout Players Invited to NBA D-League Training Camps |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html |access-date=February 4, 2013 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151218094230/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/full_list_returning_affiliate_local_tryout_players_2012.html |archive-date=December 18, 2015 }}</ref> and represented them in the 2013 D-League Showcase Three Point Shootout, finishing in second place.

On February 4, 2013, Landry was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite news|title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |access-date=February 4, 2013 |work=NBA.com |date=February 4, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065410/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |archive-date=October 22, 2013 }}</ref> and on February 16, Landry won the NBA Developmental League Three Point Shootout. On March 12, it was announced that Landry had suffered a season ending knee injury and was placed on the inactive list.<ref>{{cite news|title=Landry Done for Season|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/reno/landry_done_for_season_2013_03_12.html|access-date=March 12, 2013|work=NBA.com|date=March 12, 2013}}</ref>

Following a [[2013 NBA Summer League]] stint, Landry was signed by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in September 2013, but was waived on October 25.<ref>{{cite news|title=Los Angeles Lakers waive forward Marcus Landry|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14649|access-date=October 25, 2013|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 25, 2013}}</ref>

On December 16, 2013, Landry was re-acquired by the Reno Bighorns. On December 20, his contract was bought out by the Bighorns after just one game. On December 20, 2013, he signed with [[CB Sevilla|Cajasol Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cajasol Sevilla signs Marcus Landry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/109502/cajasol-sevilla-signs-marcus-landry.html|access-date=4 January 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=20 December 2013}}</ref>

On August 2, 2014, Landry signed with [[Basket Zaragoza 2002|CAI Zaragoza]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news|title=CAI Zaragoza agreed to terms with Marcus Landry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/130010/cai-zaragoza-agreed-to-terms-with-marcus-landry.html|access-date=August 2, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=August 2, 2014}}</ref> In 34 league games for Zaragoza in 2014–15, he averaged 10.4 points, 3.8 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.

On August 17, 2015, Landry signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-marcus-landry|title=Bucks Sign Marcus Landry |work=NBA.com|date=August 17, 2015|access-date=August 17, 2015}}</ref> He was waived by the Bucks on October 21, 2015, after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-request-waivers-three-players|title=Bucks Request Waivers on Three Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2015|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref> On December 20, he returned to the Liga ACB, this time with [[San Sebastián Gipuzkoa BC|RETAbet.es GBC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=118728|title=Marcus Landry se incorpora al RETAbet.es GBC|work=ACB.com|date=December 20, 2015|access-date=December 20, 2015|language=Spanish|archive-date=December 22, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222090019/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=118728|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 3, 2016, Landry signed with [[Basket Brescia Leonessa]] of Italy for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Germani Basket Brescia, ufficiale l'acquisto di Marcus Landry!|url=http://www.basketbrescialeonessa.it/germani-basket-brescia-ufficiale-la-firma-di-marcus-landry/|access-date=August 3, 2016|work=Basketbrescialeonessa.it|date=August 3, 2016|language=Italian}}</ref> Landry was named the [[Lega Basket Serie A MVP]] of the 2016–17 season, after averaging a league-high 19.6 points per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/234036/marcus-landry-named-serie-a-mvp-vincenzo-esposito-is-coach-of-the-year.html |title=Marcus Landry named Serie A MVP. Vincenzo Esposito is Coach of the Year |work=Sportando.com |date= 8 May 2016 |access-date= 9 May 2016}}</ref>

On September 19, 2019, Landry signed with Goyang Orions.

==Personal life==
Landry is the son of Mark and Anita and the younger brother of [[Carl Landry]], who played in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], and also has a younger sister Shenita Lasha, who is a professional basketball player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/carl_landry/|title=Carl Landry Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 21, 2015}}</ref> His wife, Efueko, played basketball at Marquette and has three children: a son, Marcus Jr., and two daughters, Mariah and Makaylah.<ref name="Badgers" />
